newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end lower, snap four-day rally.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end lower, snap four-day rally.

text.p: Toronto stocks snapped a four-day winning streak on Friday after strong U.S. economic data rekindled fears of a rise in interest rates.
The TSE 300 Composite Index fell 26.54 points to close at 6851.14, but the market recovered some of its early losses.
The key index set new closing and intraday peaks over the previous four sessions.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average also rebounded from early losses Friday, but still closed down 28 points.
"I think people were looking for an opportunity to take profits anyway," said ScotiaMcLeod director of equity trading Fred Ketchen.
The TSE sank early with U.S. stocks and bonds after the release of strong U.S. data. The U.S. jobless rate fell to a 25-year low of 4.8 percent in July from 5 percent in June.
Canadian bonds also ended sharply weaker, with the 30-year long bond off C$1.55 at C$119.95 to yield 6.408 percent.
The recovery in stock prices later in the day suggested long-term buyers were getting back into the market.
"The losses were pared back quite substantially and it seems there is a more comfortable feeling about sustaining long-term growth," Ketchen said.
Next week's trickle of earnings and economic data suggests the market is entering a period of consolidation, he said.
All but two of Toronto's 14 sub-groups ended lower. There were modest gains in energy and real estate.
Over 83 million shares were traded worth C$1.43 billion ($724 million)
Declining stocks outnumbered advances 495 to 415, with 324 issues unchanged.
* Toronto's top losers were led by George Weston Ltd., off 6.80 at 95.20 in light volume. Stampeder Exploration Ltd. dominated heavy traders, down 0.10 to 7.05 on 3.3 million shares.
* Coca-Cola Beverages Ltd. jumped 1.60 to 21.80 after parent Coca-Cola Enterprises sweetened its offer for the 52 percent public stake in the Canadian subsidiary.
* Airline Air Canada slipped 0.05 to 12 on 1.03 million shares after announcing a $1.4 billion aircraft purchase from Europe's Airbus Industrie.
